item.title: Re: Chearleader Pom Poms[Seeking Greenlight]
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via pm
Hello there!
Interesting SCP you've got here…
Would be a shame if someone…
Critiqued it…

+ show block
– hide block

So, I'm going to be honest, I love this idea. I really, really like the story, the characters, the anomaly, all that good stuff, it's perfect. So I'm going to go ahead and give you a greenlight.
However, I do have some of concerns I'd like you to take care of before going through with your idea. This is the same concern that Cybersqyd pointed out. The story is predictable, primarily because we know about the affects of the anomaly. So, the way that I'm going to suggest that you overcome this is by leaving the actual description towards the end. Maybe have the person writing the article be affected by the waves? They keep writing the wrong things? Or going off topic? Perhaps there can be 4-5 different descriptions between the addendums, and at the very end of your paper is an actual description of the anomalous properties, with an ominous ending indicating that the SCP has reeked some sort of unknown havoc onto the foundation.
Please do reach out if you have any questions about the story line/article! And keep me posted on how the article turns out. You can reach me by pm if you need help. Best of luck with the article!

item.title: Re: New author need greenlight for idea
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PMs
Sorry for the late reply
Here lies the crit:

+ show block
– hide block

Overall, while I do think this concept has potential, it's falling really flat in terms of the story. There's no narrative, no event, no character that your article revolves around. You need something more than just "This SCP did this thing and this thing and this thing". It needs to be much more detailed. For example, what may have happened if the SCP did come into contact with another SCP at one point? Maybe have a video transcript of the containment breach? Or maybe have an interview with someone who discovered it/provide some solid backstory for it? Maybe provide a log of contact with aliens? Something like that. Just spice up the story. You have a solid Foundation, but you need to build up on it from there. Unfortunately, until you create an acceptable story, I won't be able to Greenlight it. But if you would like me to take a second look, please do reach out!

item.title: "Super Cool Purpose": OK sometimes!
item.content:encoded:
If skips were never desirable. there wouldn't be so many PoIs and GoIs trying to collect them (Church of the Broken God, Scarlet King cultists, etc.) Even the grimdark artifacts tend to give some advantage that people want; and the not-so-grimdark artifacts can indeed be beneficial. (Healer skips like #500 and #2295 qualify; but so do object creators like #38 and #294, even if the latter are easier to abuse.)

As long as human beings are fallible enough to want an advantage that Those Other Guys can't duplicate — even the best-intentioned people will look for beneficial skips. As long as non-Foundation groups have enough brains to guard The Special Good Thing with every resource they can spare — those groups will Secure, Contain, and Protect whatever-it-is on their own terms.

The Foundationverse is a big place, with room for multiple genres and tones side by side. People who like gritty horror, wacky comedy, or some other kind of creative fiction can all find skips and canons they enjoy. Grimdark fans might not include anything benevolent, harmless, or likable in their headcanon. Comedy fans might not include indestructible horrors or hopeless apocalyptic scenarios in their headcanon. As long as the Foundation still takes center stage, still relies on science and research, and still cares about keeping "WTF is that?" phenomena away from average people…any well-done creation has a right to exist on this wiki. Yes, some tropes are difficult to reuse creatively after the first time; but "difficult" doesn't mean "impossible".

item.title: Re: Incorporeal mass at the center of the Earth
item.content:encoded:
Collapsed for ease of scrolling.

+ show block
– hide block

With your response and update, I’m afraid I’ve formulated further questions regarding your concept.

To start with, considering the individuals in the center of the earth wouldn’t be able to see anything, how would they (and subsequently the Foundation) know where they were? I’m rather sure geolocation is harder when you’re literally at the center of the earth; however, that’s something else that could be hand-waved away as ‘co-opted anomalous tech’.

Speaking of anomalous tech, this line confused me a bit:

A note at the end describes how the foundation isn't pursuing this avenue of research due to logistics and a lack of benefits.

If the Foundation isn’t pursuing a way to get people back from the core of the earth, then what exactly are the people on the surface doing while they’re receiving these messages?

I’m also going to ask what may sound like a bit of a weird question: why the center of the earth? It seems like any inhospitable plane of existence could be substituted in with minimal change to the plot. This tends to be a bad sign, in my experience. To give an example of this kind of problem, let’s consider the movies Toy Story and Cars. The problems faced by the protagonists in Toy Story (getting replaced, getting lost, etc.) are problems that only toys could possibly have, while the problems in Cars (getting stranded, losing the ‘big race’) are completely separate from the movie’s protagonist being a living car. As a consequence, the narrative of Toy Story feels considerably more streamlined and straightforward than Cars.

item.title: The Blind Researcher
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP article
Genre: Slightly leaning towards horror, but not really. A bit similar to Cain/Plague doctor genre.
Elevator pitch: An odd Researcher. She seems to have lived for an unnatural amount of time, possible millennia, and seems to know know everything that has happened in the past or is happening in the present, and always states that she is conducting research. She creates objects, often anomalous, for her research. These substances disappear when she has finished her research on that substance. She states that she wants to help the universe and all the universes, but refuses to divulge anything more than that on what her research
Central Narrative: A sample of a previously believed impossible to create chemical substance by geological researchers in the Gobi desert. This sample was claimed by a young blind woman in a lab coat, who appeared to be able to see despite her lack of eyes. When she was denied the request, she created another sample instead. Due to this, she was reported to the SCP. When confronted, she went willingly, saying "Hmm, this may help with my research. I always wanted to find more about some anomalies." She seems to know about the existence of every SCP and all secret information, despite never being informed. She creates anomalous objects to conduct often bizarre research on, seemingly out of nowhere, and has a journal which she records her findings on. This journal has many anomalous properties, but all that is written on it is basic, third-grade arithmetic. Though she is generally amiable and helpful, she refuses to divulge any information on what her research is, saying that the SCP researchers will not understand, except that it is for good. Every so often, she requests to meet another SCP, which is always denied.
Hook/Attention grabber: A researcher, whom no one understands what her research is, while creating bizarre anomalies in the path of her research. Also, she knows almost everything about every SCP, which creates quite a unique threat.

item.title: Robot Refugees From Outer Space
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, Action

Elevator Pitch: Three extraterrestrial lifeforms mechanical in nature claiming to be millions of years old and a machine they refer to as "The Forge" have been recently detained. Apparently they are the last remaining members of their species, and the Forge is their last hope of saving it. The Forge is a highly advanced piece of technology that is the robots' main method of reproduction, able to practically 3D print new members of their species under the correct circumstances. According to the three, Earth has the perfect conditions to incubate the Forge. However, the Forge supplies itself with the materials necessary to undergo such processes by absorbing and thaumaturgically converting large amounts of matter. Due to the catastrophic implications of letting a machine like this function on Earth, consuming the world's resources, the Foundation has concluded that the Forge must be destroyed ASAP before a GH-O 'Dead Greenhouse' Scenario could occur. There is only one problem, though: the Forge is nigh-indestructible by conventional means. But the Foundation is quickly looking into ways of solving this problem.

Central Narrative: The three aliens learn they must race against the clock to breach containment, secure the Forge, and escape the Foundation before the machine is destroyed, sealing their species' fate for good. However, if they successfully incubate the Forge on Earth, it could very well mean the end of organic life as we know it.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Readers will be intrigued by the extensive worldbuilding of the SCPs and their backstories, as well as interesting characters. They will want to find out what will happen to the Forge and the three aliens, and how the story will end. No matter whose side they're on, the story will grip them, pulling them in, compelling them to see this story to the end. Best of all, this whole narrative is neatly packaged into the clinical tone the wiki's readers know and love!

Additional Notes: I would like to hear your thoughts, suggestions, and critiques on the narrative aspect of my SCP article

item.title: Re: Humanity, for Dummies
item.content:encoded:
in demanding the papers the SCP now has to choose between the worth of the information versus the worth of the lives in question. If the information has any worth then it may be worth sacrificing those in danger to keep the information safe, especially if it involves operating information or a dangerous SCP.

I kinda considered something like that, although I wasn't as clear as I could've been. Part of that whole point was that the individuals were too valuable to be sacrificed. I mentioned the Site Director, but I also figured that important heads of research would be included. People who, due to the nature of the Foundation, might have exclusive knowledge that couldn't be written down.

But I definitely get where you're coming from. Honestly, papers/information was the best… excuse, I guess, I could find. I wanted a proper reason for the SCP to be attacking the Foundation, a motive outside of murder-monster. I also wanted a reason for the Foundation not to simply *kill* the SCP, and hostages was what I came up with. From there, my reasoning was that the SCP would have to have a reason to not kill the hostages, and… well, demanding information was the best I had. I'd love to hear any suggestions on that front, though.

you may want to start with a sympathetic SCP in the first place.

Okay this one's absolutely on me. I neglected more details on what the SCP itself was, because the narrative was the main thing I was thinking about. Basically, my thought was that the SCP is an android, either semi-biological or with an extremely advanced AI. Humanoid was the way I described it, but in retrospect that was a bad call. I'll probably change that, so thank you for making me pay attention to my word choice.

+ show block
– hide block

it becomes a lot harder for the concept if you need to create sympathy in a hardened SCP

Funny thing is, that was kind of the whole thing I was aiming for. I feel it wouldn't be as… impactful, I guess, if the SCP was sympathetic at-the-start. It seemed like a more interesting idea that, rather than bringing the humanity out of something that already had it, the Foundation would create humanity where there wasn't any, in a sense.

I feel like if the SCP is just a scared child or someone forced into doing something, I'd kind of lapse into other SCP's side-territory. From many of the SCP's I've read, the Foundation tends to treat those kinds of SCP's relatively humanely. The Reluctant Dimension Hopper springs to mind, for me.

Thank you for responding, though! I've re-assessed a lot of my concept and found some holes and things I didn't consider. I'll do a bit of editing to make my point a bit clearer.

(Uh, in a few hours though, it's late where I am right now!)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Re: Uncertain Unreality
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, what is the link between Scenario A and B besides the containment cell (which I’m assuming was constructed for the girl?). Right now, the way you’ve described both scenarios makes it seem as though both anomalies are entirely separate and they’ve only come together in a random and chance-encounter sort of way.

Right, I probably should've been more clear about it. Scenario A and B are considered, more or less the same anomaly, because as soon as someone learns of the SCP as a whole, they're randomly placed into one of the scenarios. For instance, you tell two people about SCP-XXXX, then show them the chamber. One person sees nothing, the other sees a person. At any given point in time this might randomly change, too. Now the one who saw a person now just sees nothing. They are the same anomaly all in all. And again, it's fundamentally impossible to prove which is the actual thing

Secondly, I’m having trouble believing the plausibility of the scenario. Yes, the young girl’s power might be significant, but how is she able to overwhelm the Foundation staff so easily? I’d imagine that agents would be well-equipped with amnestics and other precautions.

The real issue isn't the fact that this entity is powerful, it's the fact that n o t h i n g w o r k s. They try everything, be it mnestics, amnestics, everything. Reality anchors, hume readers, and every single time, the results seem to be fully subjective based on who views it. The whole point is that it's something that the foundation can't figure out. They can't get any semblance of accuracy, because they dont know what's accurate.
And they hate that. It's uncertainty
Again, it's either a person who makes half of the people who know of her unable to perceive her
Or a memetic hazard, which makes half the infected people perceive a person who doesn't really exist
But they have no idea which, since every point for one side has a counteracting point on the other.
It's… sorta meant to be confusing, because by the end, the readers won't know either. Because theres no way to know. It could be one or the other

I should note that part of this comes from my own personal experience. There was a time in my life where I didnt want to be considered a real person who existed. I wanted people to treat me like a myth, or a cryptid. It was a dissasociation thing, but whatever. Just something to keep in mind

That sounds really interesting and dynamic. So maybe you'll want to expand on why they cause these earthquakes in some way whether that be a flat out answer, a mostly mysterious hint, or what have you. The most interesting and probably difficult way would be for the Foundation to establish some form of agreement of peace. Remember: Secure, Contain, Protect. item.title: Ovda Regio - Aphrodite
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article/GoI

Genre (Optional): Galactic, Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): ACS header, basic layout, and exploration logs.

Elevator Pitch: Venus, a dead toxic planet believed to have no life on it, just sent signals to the SCP foundation, and no one knows who or why they did it, but they'll find out one way or another.

Central Narrative: (SCP) The SCP is currently classified as a signal, mainly because the origin is not yet located, and no one knows where it's precise location is, besides the fact it's located in the Ovda Regio, a massive landform (5280 km) located in the Aphrodite landmass. No one knows if it's a lost tribe, a massive monster, or a distress signal. Signals usually come in an unknown translation of code, and impossible to decipher.

(GoI) The team designated to the Ovda Regio is the ORET (Ovda Regio Exploration Team). They are responsible for scanning the OR in search of the origin of the signal, hoping they don't die from the harsh elements. Because of the toxic environment, limited time on the ground, and the amount of knowledge about the lands, the origin will take a very long time to locate, and has a possibility of not being found at all.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The most interesting part will 100% be the exploration logs, as there are an abundance of them, and they all are full of interesting content.

Additional Notes: If you want to know what the Ovda Regio is, here's a link. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovda_Regio

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for responding!

I intend for the MTF unit to originally only stay there to gain more Intel, however slowly come to learn that it's actually an entire race of people which are seemingly god-like. The reason they took him is because he's the first non-light entity to attempt to interact with them in all of history. Of course they know about humans, but not much as they only seem to watch earthquakes or other catastrophic events such as Volcanoes and the like.
He'd slowly figure out most of the information due to inference and suggestion from the entities.
While I haven't directly decided on this 100%, I've been considering the fact that these SCPs are actually revealed to manually move tectonic plates to cause earthquakes, which would be extremely dangerous if they're capable of doing that.
I was considering that due to the nature of the SCPs extreme difficulty to contain and high danger, the SCP Foundation could possibly attempt to even attack the entities whilst they're appearing during an earthquake to neutralize the threat of extreme magnitude seismic activity - (due to specific patterns of locations in which they appear they could possibly predict the location of the next light). That may give the MTF a choice between choosing The Foundation or SCPs. I'd have to decide which they choose from there.
This war could then tie in with the MTF which you mentioned attempting to neutralize the entities seemingly inside of an entire war between these light beings & The Foundation. I'd have to choose how that ends, however. If they're capable of just shifting tectonic plates it could end in a possible XK-Class Scenario, ending the entire world, however I don't know if my first SCP would be allowed to go that far. I'll have to think about the escalation of it a bit more.

Reply to below, as I don't want to further the thread:

You saying that gave me another possible idea that the MTF is actually a "spokesperson" for the light people, and he advocates for the peace between them and delivers messages. I'll continue to think about it as much as I can, as it'd make sense the SCP Foundation wouldn't want to engage war.

item.title: Re: Tectonic Watchers
item.content:encoded:
In the tale itself, you should probably develop in the writing who the protagonist holds allegiance to as the events unfold. Does he hold sympathy towards them, is he still set on getting them into containment, or is he just waiting it out to get away? Why are the lights telling him all this information?
When it comes to the SCP: What is the danger or interesting aspects of these lights themselves? Is this location the lights take him to also a factor in the SCP? The SCP log would benefit if it contains the Foundation's management of the damages if at all. If the foundation is entirely unable to contain, influence, or mitigate the SCP's exposure to the outside world, it just feels sort of useless to read as part of the SCP foundation unless it's tied into other portions of the foundation. I could see potential tie-ins with SCP-1000, MTF Ghost busters, MTF Mole Rats, MTF City Slickers, and MTF White Rabbits if you're comfortable with them. Make sure to include how they are managed by the foundation to the best or their ability.

item.title: Re: A Plushie Friend
item.content:encoded:
Hello!

SCP-#### would be brought home by the field agent, who, when, in tears, hugged the object, would hear a voice calming him down.

Why would the Foundation let him take it home? They never let people keep anomalies.

He would later survive a stray bullet with no damage at all while he slept, hugging the plushie. After that, the field agent would bring the object to the foundation site immediately.

Where does the stray bullet come from.

against some Groups of Interest, who would want to have SCP-#### so they could become invincible.

I don't think you need to include any GOIs, what you have so far looks good enough.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-#### would be discovered by a field agent accidentally, when a little boy hugging the object was run over by a truck and suffered no damage at all. He (the field agent) would keep an eye on the boy for some months, who seemed to have no anomalous properties.

Sounds like a fun idea, try to hide the fact that the plushie is the anomaly at first then reveal it later on, you might need to include multiple iterations of the SCP.

Honestly, I'm liking this. I'm a huge fan of friendly SCPs and this seems to be a really good idea to include some really emotional bits if you write it well.

I'm gonna Greenlight this. There is room for expansion, but it still feels like a cool idea. I like how simple it is, I see a lot of new writers try to use overly complicated ideas before their ready so this looks like a really good place to start for a first time author.

Good luck!

Also, remember you do not need a second Greenlight in order to ask for help on the #thecritters channel.

item.title: Re: How many times should I ask for a critique?
item.content:encoded:
If they leave a placeholder and a time (Such as "Will crit within 24 hours") you can PM them after the time is up to remind them. If they don't respond, don't spam them with requests. If they've critiqued your idea and you've edited it, you can PM them again to see if they'll take another look. If someone tells you no or that they're busy, stop asking them since they're probably busy or just don't want to review it. Honestly, if you act respectfully towards the people doing you a favor, they'll have no issue critiquing you further, assuming time/life/whatever allows.

I suggest PMing more people (that you think, based on the butt squad roster, will be a good fit for critting) and stopping by our Crit Chat (#thecritters, the guide I linked there will teach you everything.) There are a lot more reviewers than just the ones on the butterfly squad roster that will help out there.

I hope this helped!
